description.value: The study examined resting-state brain activity and functional connectivity after ingestion of high- and low-fat yogurts with congruent or incongruent fat labels in functional dyspepsia patients and healthy controls.

spans.text: We investigated brain activity by functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) after the ingestion of high- and low-fat foods with correct/incorrect fat information.

value: we aimed to determine the effects of fat and information of fat content (high fat and low fat) in FD patients and healthy controls

spans.text: we aimed to determine the effects of fat and information of fat content (high fat and low fat) in FD patients and healthy controls (HCs).

FD patients showed a significantly greater ALFF in the bilateral middle frontal gyrus, left middle, and right inferior occipital gyrus and a significantly lower ALFF in the left superior frontal gyrus and left middle cingulate gyrus than did HCs (all P < 0.001, FWE corrected, ).
